missed_issues: Justification accuracy <= status accuracy holds by construction: for affected cases a correct status implies the correct 'vulnerable' justification, and for not-affected cases a correct justification implies a correct status. So 'justification is harder than status for every configuration' is mechanical; the informative quantity (justification accuracy conditional on a correct not-affected call) is not reported.

Status metrics rest on 22 affected cases (recall SD 6.9 pp is about 1.5 cases). No CIs or significance tests, so the ordering among the top configurations (Opus 81.6 +/- 3.8 vs GPT-5.5 79.9 +/- 8.0; Sonnet/Kimi/DeepSeek-Pro/GLM at 70.3-72.5) is not established.

Label reliability: Fleiss' kappa 0.667 comes from only 15 calibration cases. In the scaling phase each case had one annotator plus a non-blind reviewer, so the 88.3% 'confirmed without revision' rate is anchored reviewer agreement, not independent inter-annotator agreement.

Web access was enabled during evaluation, with no web-off ablation and no audit of agents' search traces. Downstream advisories or issue threads could reveal affected status even though the expert labels are private. Appendix C only probes memorisation of source PRs (19 PRs, 2 of 9 models).

Timeouts at the 10-minute cap count as failures (MiniMax-M2.7 12.0%, Kimi K2.6 3.1%), so these models' low scores partly reflect the runtime limit. The harness ablation (Fig. 7) has no run-to-run variance, so 'Codex consistently outperforms OpenCode' for GPT-5.5 may be within noise.

Applicability slips: (a) Java is the largest subset by median LOC, not by cases (Go has 30, Java 25); (b) the paper names pom.xml/Maven only, not Gradle; (c) agent status precision ranges 62.7-88.7 (Sonnet 68.4, DeepSeek-V4-Flash 62.7), not '~75-89'. Per-language Java numbers are given only in Fig. 5 for four configurations, and the 'multi-module Java' explanation is speculative.
note: The review matches my blind scores, verdict and COI exactly, and it already catches the 70.7% majority-class floor, the by-construction SCA precision problem, the harness/model confound and precedence-label ambiguity. No claim or stance needs to change; additions are the tautological status-vs-justification gap, weak independent label agreement, untested web-access leakage, and small factual slips in the applicability text.
